VerifyCore: Biometric & Geolocation Attendance System by Ajibodu Peter Ayomide

VerifyCore is a smart attendance application designed to stop cheating and make life easier for lecturers. It solves the problem of students signing in for absent friends by using two checks at the same time: Face Scan (Biometrics): Proves the student is the one holding the phone. GPS Location (Geofencing): Proves the student is actually inside the classroom. The Backend is built with Python. It handles the heavy lifting—like recognizing faces and checking GPS coordinates—and talks to a PostgreSQL database. The Frontend (HTML, CSS, JS) is a website that accesses the user's camera and location to send data to the backend.

Grand Chronology by John Blattner

The Grand Chronology presents a method of generating templates for use with ChatGPT, options for exporting that data, and programs to verify the chat logs and parse useful metrics from the .md files of the archived data. The Grand Chronology and the ChatGPT sessions archived within it capture a snapshot of the research process during the formative years of the AI Revolution and the Intelligence Age. This template can be employed in educational and pedagogical settings for the research or exploration of any time period or event. where every session will provide enough data for an entire book on the topic. Additionally, this method could serve as a way of collecting clean data for training LLM's or as a preventive tool in plagiarism detection, as many of the template’s questions align with those frequently asked by students to chatbots or search engines.

Simple Calculator by Mohammad Mahdi Ahmadi

This project is a simple graphical calculator built using Python’s tkinter library. It performs basic arithmetic operations—addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division—through a clean and user-friendly GUI. The interface is organized using multiple frames, each responsible for specific elements like input fields, result display, and operation buttons. The program uses StringVar to manage input and output values, allowing real-time updates in the GUI. Each arithmetic operation is implemented in its own function, which converts inputs to numbers, performs the calculation, and displays the result. Error handling is implemented using try-except blocks to manage invalid inputs and division-by-zero cases, with informative message boxes shown to the user. Utility buttons like Clear (to reset all fields) and Creator (to display information about the developer) enhance usability. Buttons are linked to their functions via the command attribute and arranged neatly within the GUI. Overall, the project serves as a great introduction to Python GUI development, showcasing layout management, event-driven programming, error handling, and clean interface design. It can be extended with features such as keyboard support, scientific operations, memory functions, or calculation history.

Register page will create user to get personalizes use of the expense tracker. After creating user, user automatically logged in to the software. After Login initial page will display Monthly Expense Summary with no details. After login 2 tabs will show on header i.e. Add Transaction and History. Add Transaction page will allow user to add transactions in 2 category i.e. Income, Expense with description of the trsansaction and date of transaction. After adding trsansaction user balance will be updated and this entry will be shown in Hostory page with all details. Index page is Monthly Expense Summary, which will show details of Income and Expense monthwise with balance. Also Forget Password and Change Password for the user feature is added. Passwords will be stored in hash format.

Gemini Telegram Bot by Amirhossein Mehrdoost

This project involves creating an intelligent Telegram bot powered by Google's Gemini API, designed to interact with users through natural language conversations. The bot leverages Gemini’s advanced AI capabilities to provide real-time responses to user queries, such as answering complex questions, generating creative content (e.g., stories, poems), offering personalized recommendations, or explaining technical concepts. Built using Python and libraries like python-telegram-bot for Telegram integration and Google’s google-generativeai SDK, the bot processes user input, sends it to the Gemini API, and delivers coherent, context-aware replies. Key features could include multi-language support, session-based interactions for continuity, and error handling for API limits. This project demonstrates skills in API integration, chatbot development, and AI-driven application design, while offering a practical tool for seamless user engagement on a popular messaging platform.

CS50x 2025 Final Project Submission Form Project Title: Personal Learning Dashboard ( edX Username: Hamzanawazwato Project Description: The Personal Learning Dashboard is a web-based application that helps students and self-learners manage their educational goals. Users can register, log in, create learning goals, update their progress, and visualize it through interactive progress bars. The site is responsive and built using Flask (Python), SQLite, HTML/CSS (with Bootstrap), and JavaScript. This project is inspired by my need to organize multiple study areas in one place and track my growth efficiently. What’s in the README.md? The README.md provides a comprehensive overview of the project, including: The purpose and functionality of the application A breakdown of each file and its role in the project Major design decisions and the reasoning behind them Instructions on how to install and run the project Limitations and future improvement plans What I Learned: Through this project, I practiced and improved my skills in: Full-stack web development (Python, Flask, HTML, CSS, JavaScript) User authentication and session management Database design using SQLite Responsive UI/UX with Bootstrap Project planning, debugging, and deployment I also deepened my understanding of software design and goal-setting tools

CS50 AI Grammer Corrector by Oussama Ghedjati

## 📖 Description The Grammar Corrector Web App is a platform designed to help users improve their writing by detecting and correcting grammatical mistakes. Many people struggle with grammar, and existing tools often provide corrections without explaining why the mistake happened. This project addresses that gap by not only fixing mistakes but also teaching the user the grammar rules behind those corrections. When a user enters a text, the application uses an AI model to analyze the content. It then highlights mistakes, suggests corrections, and provides clear explanations of the grammar rules. This way, users can learn as they write, turning errors into opportunities for improvement. The corrections are shown side by side with the original text so users can easily compare their writing with the suggested improvements. Another important feature of the application is the history system. Every time a user submits text, the original version, corrected version, and the chosen language are saved. Users can return later to review their submissions, track progress, and better understand recurring mistakes they make. Over time, this history helps learners reflect on their improvement and identify areas they need to focus on. The main purpose of this project is not just to provide instant grammar corrections, but to build a tool that supports long-term language learning. By combining correction with explanation, the app empowers users to become more confident writers. In the future, additional features such as real-time corrections, support for more languages, and personalized feedback could make the app even more powerful.

Car System This is my final project for CS50. I decided to make a simple Car Management System that runs in the terminal. Basically, it lets me keep track of cars in a small CSV database. I wanted something easy to use but still with enough commands to show I can work with files, arguments, and saving data. What it can do Add a new car (make, model, year, owner, notes) List all cars in a table Show the details of one car by its ID Delete a car by ID Search cars by keyword (like “Toyota” or owner name) Import / Export cars from/to CSV files Clear the database (reset) The data is stored in a file called cars.csv. Each car has an auto-incrementing id so you can find and delete them easily.

Finance Tracker by Swasti Kumari

For my final project, I built a web-based Personal Finance Tracker using Flask, SQLite, HTML/CSS, and JavaScript. The goal of this project is to help users manage their personal finances more effectively. Users can create an account, log in securely (with passwords hashed using Argon2), and then start tracking their money. The app lets users look up real-time stock quotes, buy and sell shares, and view a detailed history of all their transactions. It keeps their portfolio up to date automatically based on their activity. To make the app more useful, I integrated the Financial Modeling Prep API for accurate stock data and the Exchangerate.host API for currency conversion, so users can see their portfolio in different currencies. I also added features like savings goals, budget categories, and spending reports, which are displayed with interactive charts to help users visualize where their money is going. The design is clean and responsive, thanks to Bootstrap, and I included a dark mode, animated transitions, and modern icons to give it a polished feel. All data is stored in a local SQLite database, and the app is organized into separate files for routes, templates, and static content to keep the code clean and maintainable. This project builds on CS50’s Finance problem set but goes much further by solving real-world problems and providing a better user experience.

NPS and Sentiment Analyzer (Portuguese Language) by Silene Bonfante Garcia Barcaro

This project is the NPS and Sentiment Analyzer, a web application built with Python and Flask. Its main objective is to automate customer feedback analysis, transforming large volumes of raw data into actionable business insights. The primary motivation was to solve the inefficiency and inaccuracy of manual comment analysis. The system handles two pillars of analysis: (1) Real-time Sentiment Analysis of Portuguese texts, classifying them as Positive, Neutral, or Negative; and (2) Bulk NPS Calculation, processing entire files to generate the Net Promoter Score metric. For the sentiment analysis in Portuguese, I utilized the Hugging Face (Transformers) library with a specific BERT model. I overcame the challenge of achieving precision by employing a hybrid system that combines artificial intelligence with a rule-based fallback logic based on strong keywords, guaranteeing 100% accuracy in extreme cases. The final solution offers data visualization via Matplotlib (for the NPS evolution graph) and includes a secure authentication system. The project demonstrates proficiency in web development, data analysis, and the practical application of AI.

Calculator by parham ebrahimi

Hi! This is my Python program. It asks for two numbers: Y and X. Then it checks which number is bigger. If X is bigger than Y, it shows X minus Y and the result. If Y is bigger than X, it shows Y minus X and the result. For example: if X is 10 and Y is 5, it shows: 10 - 5 = 5 and says 'X is bigger.' If Y is 8 and X is 3, it shows: 8 - 3 = 5 and says 'Y is bigger.' The program uses f-strings to display the math problems. This project helped me learn about user input, if conditions, and string formatting in Python.

"Python Calculator: A Simple and Interactive Arithmetic Tool" by Nour Salah Elhabashi

The Python Calculator Project is a simple yet effective program that allows users to perform basic arithmetic operations like addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division. Built using Python, the calculator prompts users to input two numbers and an operator, then displays the result. It includes error handling to manage invalid inputs, such as non-numeric values or division by zero. The program runs in a loop, enabling users to perform multiple calculations without restarting, and offers an option to exit. This project demonstrates core Python concepts like input handling, conditionals, loops, and error management, making it an excellent beginner-friendly exercise.
